fact: The Government of Ghana, with UNESCO and the EU, launched an AI literacy training programme for 240 Civil Service staff to serve as trainers in their institutions, and the Head of the Civil Service urged HR directors to build AI literacy into onboarding.

The Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, with UNESCO, launched an AI literacy programme for civil servants; the first three-day cohort ran 24-26 March 2026, with four cohorts planned through May on a training-of-trainers model for ministries, departments and agencies.

fact: The Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation says the 2024 DigSMART Scale-Up, run with the Office of the Head of Civil Service and the Tony Blair Institute, trained 830 participants from 42 ministries, departments and agencies in three centres (Accra, Sunyani, Bolgatanga), after a 2023 pilot of 170 with a 70 percent graduation rate.

Graphic Online reports that 520 public and civil servants (262 officers, 207 managers, 51 leaders) from 53 ministries, departments and agencies graduated from the DigSMART Scale-Up programme, a four-month course from February to May 2024 run by the Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation.
Communication Minister Samuel Nartey George announced an initiative to train 200,000 civil servants in AI, digital governance and coding under the One Million Coders Programme.
